destination.name: Wentworth
destination.tagline: A Murray River town at the junction of the Darling and Murray rivers.
destination.description: Wentworth is a small town in the far south-west of New South Wales where the Darling River meets the Murray. Junction Park has a 35-step tower over the confluence, where the waters show different colours. West of town, the Perry Sandhills are 160 hectares of shifting dunes, and the Old Wentworth Gaol, built from bricks made on site in 1879–81, is open for self-guided visits.
whyVisit: Watch the Darling meet the Murray
Walk the Perry Sandhills' shifting dunes

goodToKnow.title: Gaol is closed Thursday and Friday
goodToKnow.detail: Old Wentworth Gaol is open Mon–Wed 10 am–4 pm and Sat–Sun 10 am–2 pm; entry about $8.

goodToKnow.title: Sandhills are 6 km out
goodToKnow.detail: Perry Sandhills are 6 km west of town, open 24 hours and free; there is little shade, so go early in hot weather.

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat
goodToKnow.detail: Summers are hot (record 48.6 °C), so plan outdoor visits for spring or autumn.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} avoid the hot summers of this semi-arid corner and suit the dunes and river walks.
